title: Drinking Water with Meals Could Make You Eat More
paragraphs: Many people believe that drinking water with a meal will help them feel full and eat less. However, a new study from the United States suggests that it may actually have the opposite effect.

The study was led by Paige Cunningham of Cornell University and published in the journal Appetite in 2026. It involved 49 healthy adults. Each person chose a meal of either chicken tikka masala or beef chili, which was served with water. The researchers recorded the participants on video while they ate.

The researchers found that the more water people drank, the more food they ate. For every 100 grams of water that people drank, they ate an extra 39 grams of food, which is about 49 calories. In addition, people who switched more often between eating and drinking ate more food.

Why might this happen? The researchers have several ideas. First, water leaves the stomach quickly, so it probably does not make people feel full for long. Second, water may make food easier to swallow, which can make people eat faster. Third, eating the same food again and again usually makes it less enjoyable. However, drinking water between bites may clean the mouth and make the next bite taste fresh again, so people keep eating.
Surprisingly, people who drank water quickly ate less food overall. The researchers are not sure why.

However, the study had limitations. It was a new analysis of data that had already been collected, so it only shows a link between drinking water and eating more. It does not prove that water causes people to eat more. Cunningham said that follow-up research is now being done, and a new trial at Cornell is testing whether water with meals changes how much adults eat.
